about: The root-cause clusters of the accessibility findings ledger (lib/a11y-issues.mjs; tests/AGENTS.md, A11y: the findings ledger and the cluster catalog). A cluster has id, title, an optional tracker (a task id, or a list of them; code, never printed on the page) and match rules: source, then any of checks, kinds, rules, causes, criteria, pages, themes, where, axeIssues. Values in a field are ORed, fields in a rule ANDed, rules in a cluster ORed. A finding no rule matches lands in needs-triage; one that two rules match fails lib/__tests__/a11y-issues.test.mjs. triageLimit is the exact number of sampled findings that need triage: it only goes down.

clusters.title: The overlay clones split the accessibility tree: the column headers read after the data, each row is exposed twice, the row headers sit apart from their rows, and a screen reader loses the cell's row index
The grid is built from divs with ARIA roles, and its treegrid root holds children the role does not allow
The focus is not returned to the cell after Escape, Enter or a shortcut closes an editor, a menu or the comment editor, and a screen reader does not re-announce the cell

Controls without an accessible name or role: the editor inputs, the native date and time inputs, the select editor, the comment textarea, the filter listbox, the autocomplete list, and the focus catchers
Menu items have no menu parent, the highlighted item carries aria-selected, separators are exposed as menu items, and a screen reader hears the context menu as a table
The accessible name of the Filters "Filter by value" component does not include its visible text
The Filters "Select all" and "Select none" controls are buttons nested inside buttons
Text, icon, checkbox, grid line and focus indicator contrast under 4.5:1 or 3:1 per theme, and a focus indicator that does not show
Drags without a single-pointer or keyboard alternative that does all the drag does, and controls that act on the press or after the pointer left

Content cut off or needing a sideways scroll at 320 px or 200 %, hover content that does not dismiss, controls drawn over each other, a locked orientation, and motion that runs on or ignores the reduced-motion preference
In forced colors the focus, the selected range, the highlighted menu item, the header icons or the grid lines are not drawn
A range extension, a sort and a nested row's level are not announced: no status message reaches the screen reader
Tab walks out of an open modal dialog to the content behind it, which the dialog hides from assistive technology
Pagination and sheets bar buttons, links and checkboxes are smaller than 24 by 24 px, or sit closer than that to their neighbors
VoiceOver names no row number on a cell move, and no column number in WebKit, on a well-formed grid too: the screen reader's behavior, not the grid's (the scenario notes record it)
With autoWrapRow a Tab walk wraps rows and leaves the grid through Ctrl+End then Tab, as the shortcut guide documents
A page has no tab-order or accessibility-tree golden recorded yet
Column headers with no accessible name: the corner and the empty header cells label their cells with nothing
axe's experimental hidden-content rule lists every hidden element for review: the overlay clones' hidden rows, the closed editors and menus
The scrolling holder is not keyboard focusable, though every cell in it is: axe cannot tell and lists it for review
